one_line: Clarksdale grew on sharecropping (94% of farmers were tenants in 1930). The first all-machine cotton crop was grown at Hopson just south of town in 1944, the 1967 Senate hunger tour ended there, and white students left for Lee Academy in 1970. The county has lost 57% of its people since 1950, and its life expectancy is now 65.3 years against 77.1 for the U.S.
biggest_caveat: Middle decades unconfirmed (Cooper Tire closure date/jobs, hospital history, casino jobs); Holley argues migration also drove mechanization; coded micro, not rural.

dropped_tracts.28027950100: Coahoma County MS across the river

one_line: Elaine's sharecroppers organized in 1919 and were met with a massacre that led to Moore v. Dempsey (1923); machines, timber decline and plant closures then emptied Phillips and Lee counties, with the steepest 2000s population loss of any metro or micro area.
biggest_caveat: Arkansas, not Mississippi; 7 tracts spread 50 miles over two counties; history rows must be rebuilt without the MS tract; Mohawk Rubber closure single-sourced.

why: Matches the Mississippi Delta request; compact, stable tracts; dated anchors (Hopson 1944, hunger tour 1967, Lee Academy 1970); worst county life expectancy of the three. R030 is backup.

dropped_tracts.55079008900: in 53210, Metcalfe Park; 101 adult correctional GQ

one_line: A white working-class area rated 'declining' in the 1930s filled with Black families pushed north by 1960s freeway clearance, just before the A.O. Smith frame plant inside it fell from a reported 10,000 jobs to 300 at its 2006 closing and the ZIP became UW-Milwaukee's 'ground zero' for the imprisonment of Black men.
biggest_caveat: Only 4 of 8 tracts mostly in 53206; mostly HOLC C not D; 'most incarcerated ZIP' not supported (PolitiFact 2019).

one_line: Central took Cleveland's Great Migration newcomers, was graded 98% 'Hazardous', got the nation's first federal public housing on those same blocks, then lost nearly half its people in the 1960s as urban renewal and factory decline hit.
biggest_caveat: Narrowed to two tracts (~5,600 people); biggest drop before 1970.

one_line: On Blue Hill Avenue, a 1938 'declining' grade, the 1950s move of Jewish families and institutions, the 1967 Grove Hall unrest and the 1968 B-BURG loan zone, followed by 1,200+ foreclosures, line up with Grove Hall losing 25% of its people and unemployment rising from 6.5% to 16.5% between 1970 and 1990.
biggest_caveat: Tracts already 94.5% Black in 1970; B-BURG hit Mattapan harder; the 33-year life expectancy gap headline is Nubian Square vs Back Bay, not Grove Hall (Grove Hall gap 1.4-4.6 years).

added_tracts.06037243100: SE Watts; Imperial Courts ~1/3 of homes, run with and without

one_line: In a two-square-mile Watts hemmed in by covenants and graded red in 1939, three housing projects, the 1965 uprising, South LA plant closures (12,000 jobs, 1975-86), a freeway fight and a 2007 hospital closure piled up, while the Black share fell from 91% (1970) to 23% (2020).
biggest_caveat: Rebuilt Watts sits near the 25th income and 24th health percentile, outside the screen; Black-to-Latino change means trends compare different people.

dropped_tracts.48141003602: juvenile detention center, not in either neighborhood

one_line: Repeated takings packed the border's main immigrant gateway into fewer, worse homes: 1916 cleanup (100+ homes), 1946-47 Paisano widening (up to 6,000 displaced), 1963-67 Chamizal (5,600+), tenement clearance; then El Paso apparel jobs fell 92% from 1990 to 2019. Every graded area was HOLC D.
biggest_caveat: Census series starts after most clearance; poverty peaked 1990 before NAFTA; life expectancy 76.3 not low; poor health rests on modeled rates.

one_line: 1937 D grades, the 1965-77 St. John clearance for I-475 and Buick (Black homeownership 50% to 15%), GM Flint jobs ~80,000 to under 8,000, Buick City closed 1999, state takeovers 2002 and 2011, the 2014 water switch; the area lost half its people 1990-2020.
biggest_caveat: St. John core mostly outside these tracts; cluster only 47% Black; usable census from 1990; GM figures need primary sources.

added_tracts.46102941200: Kyle; completes Oglala Lakota County; income alone would fail screen

one_line: The poorest, shortest-lived county in IHME's 1980-2014 series sits on Oglala Lakota land that shrank in dated steps: the 1868 treaty, the 1877 Black Hills taking, the 1889 breakup and the 1910 Bennett County opening; IHS underfunding and Whiteclay alcohol sales came later, and tribal institutions answered.
biggest_caveat: Poor at every point with data, not a decline from a high; life expectancy rose 61.3 to 66.8 while the gap with the U.S. held near 12 years; census undercount.

one_line: For 50 years coal under Black Mesa paid tribal budgets and drew down the N-aquifer while federal land rulings relocated more than 3,600 Navajo and Hopi families; the 2005 and 2019 closures cut about 700 jobs and 23% of Navajo revenue, and a quarter of homes still lack complete plumbing.
biggest_caveat: No matching health series; boundaries unstable before 2000; overlaps coal theme.

why: County-matched IHME life expectancy (lowest in nation), stable tracts, every land loss dated in treaty, statute or Supreme Court record.

dropped_tracts.01073002402: south of rail yards; 2010 parent also covers 24.01

one_line: In North Birmingham, convict labor, racial zoning, HOLC D grades and the loss of steel and pipe jobs piled up around coke plants still inside the tract lines, ending in arsenic, lead and benzo(a)pyrene in hundreds of yards, a Superfund proposal that never became a listing, and a 2018 federal bribery conviction over fighting it.
biggest_caveat: ATSDR found current air exposures unlikely to cause harm; county found 2000-2009 cancer, asthma, COPD deaths no different from rest of county. Rebuild history on 4 tracts.

one_line: Before Katrina, the back of the Upper Ninth and Seventh wards was walled in one layer at a time: the Industrial Canal (1923), HOLC D grades, the Florida (1946) and Desire (1956) projects on swamp and dump land, homes and a school on the Agriculture Street dump, and I-10 (1966-68). Population was already down 19% from 1990 to 2000 before the storm cut it nearly in half.
biggest_caveat: Agriculture St landfill/Gordon Plaza (137.01) and Claiborne strip sit just outside kept tracts; many dates rest on Wikipedia; 1970-80 fit ~0.18.

one_line: In a melon and sugar beet town, the 1974 end of federal sugar quotas, the 1979 sugar plant closing, and the 1980s sale of its ditch water to Aurora (about 7,500 acres dried, per the local water district) came before food jobs fell by about half (1987-94) and the population fell 21% from its 1960 peak.
biggest_caveat: Aurora sale figures UNCONFIRMED; tract holds only 61% of town (south side in 9682); candidates.csv mislabels tract as 9685; ACS 2008-12 owner share copies 2010 census.

one_line: In a cannery town, the can plant closed (1986), county factory jobs fell 47% (2000-2011), most working residents commuted out, and there was no addiction treatment or HIV clinic in town; then injected oxymorphone set off the 2015 HIV outbreak (188 cases by April 2016).
biggest_caveat: Cannery never went dark; county factory jobs recovered to 2,544 by 2022; earlier cuts thin; owner shares disagree 10-17 points.

dropped_tracts.54047954503: FCI McDowell 1,881 of 4,755; also removes downtown Welch and Kimball

one_line: Once the top coal county in the U.S., McDowell fell from 98,887 people in 1950 to 19,111 in 2020 as mechanization, U.S. Steel leaving Gary, the 2001-02 floods, the pill wave (~96 pills per resident per year, 2006-12) and the 2016 Walmart closing came one after another.
biggest_caveat: Prison drop removes downtown Welch and Kimball; U.S. Steel exit year and 1950s job counts secondary only.

one_line: Owsley County's small burley farms and commuting coal wages carried a county that lost 55% of its people after 1940; the 2004 end of the tobacco quota left no recorded tobacco, 84 farms and negative farm income, while poverty stayed above 30% for 35 years.
biggest_caveat: Kept tract 9301 life expectancy near average (77.3); short-lived 9302 (66.5) not in candidate; decline began 1940s not 1980s.

why: Deeper decline (-81% vs -64%), more dated cuts each with a county series, uses PLACES 2025.

added_tracts.30093000101: other half of 2010 tract 1; fit ~0.95 to 1990

one_line: Butte's Uptown lost its company, its underground mines, its smelter and its east side neighborhoods over 70 years, then lived beside a filling acid pit and a cleanup still growing: EPA cut the lead standard to 456 ppm in Sept 2026 and added 7,000+ properties.
biggest_caveat: Adding 1.01 dilutes depth (poverty 28.5% vs 39.6%); tract poverty flat near one third since 1990; big losses predate tract data. Pumps off April 22, 1982.

one_line: In a cotton county seat that lost 60% of its people by 1970, a federal court found public housing assigned by race (1983); three local banks failed (1985-90), school enrollment fell 64%, and the hospital closed in 2014; old tract has the county's shortest life expectancy (71.3).
biggest_caveat: ACS poverty only 13-15%, down from 28.6% in 1990; income MOE +/- $19,915; pick rests on noisy estimates.

dropped_tracts.39113060200: Drexel CDP, outside Dayton and HOLC area, best health in cluster

one_line: West Dayton's Black west side was redlined (tract 1651 is 77% grade D), shaken by the 1966 unrest on West Fifth St., cut by US-35 (283 homes on one 1.4-mile stretch), then hit by the Delphi, GM and NCR exits in 2008-09, a county overdose rate from 22 to 82 per 100,000, and the 2018 Good Samaritan closing; Westwood fell from 9,069 people in 1990 to 4,433 in 2020.
biggest_caveat: GM Moraine, NCR, Good Samaritan outside tracts (county level only); job counts UNCONFIRMED; DeSoto Bass may sit partly in tract 41.

dropped_tracts.17031340600: Wentworth Gardens 84% of tract; Armour Square, White Sox park

one_line: Englewood and Fuller Park were graded D almost wall to wall; the Dan Ryan (1961-62) split Fuller Park, the stockyards closed in 1971, no new housing from 1969 to 2004, 63rd and Halsted lost its anchors after 1978, four high schools closed in 2018; the two areas fell from 114,769 people at their peaks to 26,936 in 2020.
biggest_caveat: Life expectancy rose 1990-2010 (62.4 to 70.7), so a lasting gap not a decline; key Fuller Park facts secondhand.

dropped_tracts.25025080601: commercial core, bus station, Madison Park HS, 2,484 dorm residents

one_line: BPHC's lowest life expectancy tract in Boston (tract 803: 68.8 vs 91.6 in Back Bay 107.02, 2015-2021). Both tracts graded D in 1938, Inner Belt land cleared at their north edge before the 1970-72 cancellation, Lower Roxbury urban renewal, the Washington St El left in 1987 (sales at the square fell 30%) and a bus replaced it in 2002, Orchard Park rebuilt through HOPE VI, displacement pressure now.
biggest_caveat: About two-thirds of homes subsidized, so low income partly reflects income limits; 387 unidentified GQ in 804.01; USALEEP gives tract 803 76.9 vs BPHC 68.8.
vs_grove_hall: Nubian better: actual BPHC headline tract, dated public actions; Grove Hall gap only 1.4-4.6 years.

one_line: Shelley v. Kraemer house (4600 Labadie, tract 1101, HOLC C13) inside kept tracts; sourcing from court opinions, state archives, Census, Mapping Inequality (56% D, eastern tracts), Colin Gordon's 2009 report on covenants, Real Estate Exchange zones, FHA, Mill Creek relocation, Homer G. Phillips.
biggest_caveat: The Ville proper, Homer G. Phillips (1113) and Pruitt-Igoe site (1275) are adjacent tracts not in the set; Greater Ville half graded mostly C and B; history must be rebuilt.

one_line: Primary record for each redlining step: 1910 ordinance (DOJ 2016 report), 87.5% HOLC D by overlay (7 of 8 tracts 98-100% D), Thompson v. HUD findings naming Gilmor Homes, Murphy Homes and Harlem Park scattered sites, city count of 971 homes and 62 businesses cleared for the highway, 1968 unrest blocks in a University of Baltimore archive, Health Department life expectancy 4-5 years below the city.
biggest_caveat: Neighborhood stats are for CSAs larger than tracts; 1700 block of Presbury (Freddie Gray arrest) in tract 1502, just outside; tract 1604 graded C; Power and Pietila books not opened.

one_line: The 1928 covenant behind Hansberry v. Lee covered exactly tracts 4205 and 4206; the Hansberry house at 6140 S. Rhodes is in 4206; HOLC D78 notes quote the Illinois Supreme Court ruling upholding the covenant; University of Chicago records show it paid part of the covenant's legal defense; all five tracts 75-100% D; life expectancy ~73 vs 82.6 in Hyde Park.
biggest_caveat: South Campus, Green Line demolition and Obama Center price rise are east of Cottage Grove, outside tracts; University's $83,597 covenant spending second-hand from Hirsch.
